title: Calculating sample size and test duration

videos.script: How many visitors does a test need? The honest answer is a calculation, and it takes four numbers. {{four}} How often people convert today. The smallest improvement worth finding. How often you will accept a false alarm. And how often you are willing to miss a real effect. {{inputs}} Give it those, and the arithmetic returns a number of visitors. For Panela's checkout, about nineteen thousand in each group. {{answer}} Then the traffic turns visitors into days, and the calendar turns days into whole weeks. {{days}} The number surprises people, because it is big. And it has one property everybody should know. Halve the improvement you want to detect, and you need four times the visitors. {{quarter}} That single fact decides more tests than any formula. It is why small changes need big companies, and why a team with little traffic should test bold ideas. {{bold}} This lesson does the calculation by hand, checks it with statsmodels, and turns it into a date in the calendar. {{end}}
